findings.evidence: prodMulEquivRight_apply = `FundamentalGroup.map ContinuousMap.fst`; prodMulEquivLeft_apply = `FundamentalGroup.map ContinuousMap.snd`. Mathlib uses `prodUnique`/`uniqueProd` (word order), not a Left/Right suffix, to encode which factor is trivial.
findings.fix: Name by the surviving/projected factor to match `Prod.fst`/`Prod.snd` and the `_apply` lemmas: `prodMulEquivFst` (projects to X, needs Y simply connected) and `prodMulEquivSnd` (projects to Y, needs X simply connected). Failing that, swap the suffixes so `Left`↔`fst` and `Right`↔`snd`.
findings.issue: `FundamentalGroup.prodMulEquivRight : π₁(X × Y) ≃* π₁(X)` is implemented by `ContinuousMap.fst` (the left/first projection, per `prodMulEquivRight_apply`), while `prodMulEquivLeft : π₁(X × Y) ≃* π₁(Y)` uses `snd` (the right projection). The suffix names the discarded (simply connected) factor, but a reader naturally reads `…Right` as the right-factor projection (π₁(Y)); the name and the `fst`/`snd` it wraps point in opposite directions, so the two are easy to confuse.

summary: The Left/Right suffixes on the two new projection equivalences are inverted relative to the projection they implement: `prodMulEquivRight` projects to the left factor via `fst` and `prodMulEquivLeft` to the right factor via `snd`, a misleading interface. Other names correctly describe their conclusions and mirror the circle API.
